text:
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): Hey team, urgent — our Private deployment in eu-west lost connectivity to Redwood private endpoint after we pushed an ExpressRoute routing change ~10:00 UTC. API calls hit 504s and TLS handshakes time out. Customer traffic to model endpoint resolves to 10.2.4.5 but TCP connects reset. Impacting production.
Sam (Support): @Maria @Devon escalating. Jonas, can you paste the traceroute / dig + any tcpdump you grabbed? Also include the session id shown in the app (sess=acme-9f2).
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): Dig and curl from a customer VM:
```
dig @10.0.0.2 model.redwood-private.acme.internal A +short
10.2.4.5

curl -v https://model.redwood-private.acme.internal:443/health
* Connected to 10.2.4.5 (10.2.4.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Connection reset by peer
```
They also ran traceroute: `traceroute -n 10.2.4.5` stops at their ExpressRoute PE (10.100.1.1). I attached a 20s tcpdump showing incoming SYN then RST from 10.2.4.5.
Sam (Support): Per the tcpdump the reset seems to come from our side. @deploy-bot can you confirm if any config changes or rollouts to the private control plane around 10:00 UTC?
deploy-bot: Rollout check: no customer-facing control-plane changes between 09:45-10:15 UTC. Maintenance window: none.
Maria (Network Eng): Looking at BGP/peering logs — I see a route withdrawal for prefix 10.2.4.0/24 at 2287654001 and a re-advert at 2287654065. During the withdrawal our MXes sent TCP RSTs for existing flows. Was there an intentional BGP flap on the customer's side?
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): We made a change to their ExpressRoute filter at ~10:00 to remove a /24 they thought was unused. They didn't expect that prefix to be used by Redwood endpoints.
Maria (Network Eng): That explains it — if their route filter incorrectly removed the prefix we host, traffic would blackhole until re-advertised. Two things to confirm: (1) are our private endpoints using that exact /24 (10.2.4.0/24)? (2) Are there any firewall egress rules on customer side that drop inbound established flows during route churn?
Devon (Infra Oncall): Checked endpoint VMs and the private gateway (10.2.4.5) — service alive locally, cert is valid: `x509: OK (CN=model-prod, issuer=redwood-intermediate)`. But we see TCP RSTs coming from our NAT gateway (10.2.4.1) when upstream route disappears — NAT tears sessions when next-hop goes missing.
Sam (Support): Two-pronged mitigation: ask customer to temporarily re-add the removed prefix to restore BGP advertisement, and we’ll add a hold-down/static route on our side to avoid session tears while they correct their filters. Jonas can you re-add and confirm?
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): Re-added /24 at 10:07 UTC. BGP shows prefix back by 10:08. After that, we still saw TLS handshake failures for a short window. curl now shows: `SSL: certificate verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` for some requests. Not consistent across VMs.
Maria (Network Eng): The intermittent cert verify errors likely due to OCSP/CRL checks failing during the outage — our endpoints attempt to fetch OCSP via egress to `ocsp.redwood-internal` and if that fails some clients (with strict validation) will break. Check egress allowlist: do you allow outbound to our OCSP responder (IP 52.48.12.53) on 80/443?
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): They had a strict egress allowlist; OCSP host wasn't on it. We added 52.48.12.53:443 and 52.48.12.53:80 and opened UDP 53 to their DNS resolver.
Devon (Infra Oncall): Also noticed customer NAT / firewall had a short-lived policy that resets established TCP connections when route next-hop disappears — that behavior caused many handshakes to fail. Recommended config: allow ESTABLISHED connections to persist for 120s during route churn, and permit egress to our cert/ocsp endpoints.
Sam (Support): Action items:
- Jonas: confirm BGP stable and keep /24 advertised (they did).
- Jonas: confirm egress allowlist includes OCSP and DNS to their resolver (they updated it).
- Maria/Devon: add a static /32 host route for 10.2.4.5 on our edge for 5m hold-down to prevent NAT session teardown during customer route flaps.
- Devon: rotate VPN/PSK if any suspected secret exposure? Not needed here but recommended post-incident.
Maria (Network Eng): Implemented temporary static route at 2287654325 (5m). BGP status shows stable.
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): After re-add + allowlist changes, all tests green: `curl https://model.redwood-private.acme.internal/health` returns 200, TLS handshake OK, and no 504s for 5+ minutes. Customer reports production traffic resumed.
Sam (Support): Great — we've documented the root cause as customer route-filter removed our /24 causing BGP withdrawal and NAT session resets, plus missing egress allowlist for OCSP/DNS that extended TLS failures. Jonas, please open a change control to prevent accidental removal of our prefixes and share with your network ops.
Jonas (AcmeCorp SRE): Will do — raised change ticket NET-1129 and added our prefix to a protected list. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Sam (Support): Marking as resolved on our side. If any regression please re-open. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
